text:
sophia chen: hey folks — first week here, trying to curl internal-ci.redwood.local and it times out. curl http://10.10.4.12 works but hostname doesn't resolve. macbook (Ventura). any onboarding DNS quirks i missed?

matt h: welcome! usually internal domains are resolved via the split-tunnel DNS provided by the bastion. quick checks: can you paste the output of `scutil --dns` or `/etc/resolv.conf`? also, do you see a file under /etc/resolver/ for our internal domain?

sophia chen: paste below — i stripped some lines for privacy:
```
$ scutil --dns
DNS configuration
resolver #0
  search domain[0] : redwood.com
  nameserver[0] : 1.1.1.1
resolver #7
  domain   : internal-ci.redwood.local
  nameserver[0] : 10.10.4.2
  flags    : Request A records
```
No /etc/resolver/redwood.local file present.

alyssa d: chrome on mac can use DNS-over-HTTPS and bypass the system resolver; that often explains curl working (system) but browser failing. Are you seeing failures only in browser or in apps generally?

sophia chen: both — chrome can't resolve ci host but i can ssh to ip. terminal tools like dig against system nameserver also fail unless i point at 10.10.4.2 explicitly.

matt h: ok — two things to try: create a resolver file so macOS routes that suffix to the internal nameserver, and flush the cache. run as sudo: `echo \"nameserver 10.10.4.2\" > /etc/resolver/internal-ci.redwood.local` (or just `internal-ci.redwood.local` depending on how you want suffixes handled). then `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache && sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder`

gopal r: also check chrome://settings/security -> Use secure DNS. If it's set to a public DoH provider (Cloudflare/Google), temporarily turn it off so chrome uses the system resolver. Some versions ignore /etc/resolver when DoH is enabled.

bastion-bot: New bastion route pushed for user sophia. Added route for 10.10.0.0/16 via bastion-host-3 at 2065432145.

sophia chen: created /etc/resolver/internal-ci.redwood.local with nameserver 10.10.4.2 and ran the flush commands. chrome still couldn't resolve until I toggled secure DNS off. after that, hostname resolves in browser and terminal. thanks!

matt h: nice. for permanent fix we'll update our VPN client profile to push the resolver file automatically for macs on split-tunnel. can you share which VPN client you're on (built-in, wireguard, other)?

sophia chen: using the corporate client (wireguard wrapper).

alyssa d: i'll add a short section to the onboarding doc: \"Mac: If internal hostnames don't resolve, add /etc/resolver/<suffix> pointing at 10.10.4.2 and disable browser DoH, then flush DNS.\" tagging infra to automate in the client profile.

matt h: tagging eng-infra. @gopal r can you follow up on pushing resolver rules for wireguard wrapper?

gopal r: yep, i'll take it and loop in infra this week. thanks for the clear repro steps, @sophia chen — that helps.

sophia chen: thanks everyone — saved my first-day panic :relieved:
